subject: Problem using reshape package in large data frames

messages.author: 42cb5f0c3e90d26f
messages.subject: Problem using reshape package in large data frames
parts:
Hello everyone!

I’m having a problem in casting a data frame with the reshape package.
I have an original data set of species abundances in replicate samples
at certain sites, with the following form:

SITE SP R1 R2 R3

I A 1 3 0

I B 2 5 1

I C 1 0 2

II A 4 2 0

II C 1 0 0

II D 6 3 3


Please notice that site II does not have species B and has a new
species D, the remaining two are shared with site I.
I need to get these data in the form of a matrix like:

SITE.REPLICATE A B C D

I.1 1 2 1 NA

I.2 3 5 0 NA

I.3 0 1 2 NA

II.1 4 NA 1 6

II.2 2 NA 0 3

II.3 0 NA 0 3


Using the above “toy data” in R, everything works fine using melt and
recast as follows (lets call test to may initial matrix):

> testm <- melt (test, id.var=c(“SITE”,”SPECIES”))

> testc <- cast(testm, ...~SPECIES)

> testc

SITE variable A B C D

1 I Replicate1 1 2 1 NA

2 I Replicate2 3 5 0 NA

3 I Replicate3 0 1 2 NA

4 II Replicate1 4 NA 1 6

5 II Replicate2 2 NA 0 3

6 II Replicate3 0 NA 0 3


However, when I use the same code in my real data set which is
considerably larger (73 sites and 7 replicates for site, resulting in
a molten matrix of 14469 x 4), the cast function does some kind of
aggregation (in fact it advices of an aggregation using the default
fun.aggregate) that I was not able to understand. I also tried to
split my original data frame in order to get smaller molten matrices;
it worked fine for a molten matrix smaller than 1500 rows but not for
one with 2541 rows. Does anyone know if it is a bug, or am I doing
something wrong?

(I use R 2.8.1 for Windows)

Thank you very very much in advance!

Cheers,

Dulce

messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Re: Problem using reshape package in large data frames
parts:
> the cast function does some kind of
> aggregation (in fact it advices of an aggregation using the default
> fun.aggregate) that I was not able to understand.

I probably means that somewhere, you have a data that's repeated in
your original table, such as:

...

I A 4 2 0

...

So, when converting it to the other format there are two numbers to
put in the cell determined by (Site I + Replicate 1, Species A), here
1 and 4, and cast needs an "aggregating" function to know what to do
with those (sum them, compute their mean or, by default, just count
them).

In other words, I don't think your problem comes from the length of
the data frames, but rather from the content. And with a 1500 lines
data frame you do not have duplicates while with a longer one you get
them.

I would compute a new column with the interaction of the site and
species factors (I can't remember the function to compute the
intersection right now) and I would search for duplicates with the
duplicated() function.

Hope that helps.

JiHO
